ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors and authorised signatories against: (1) SECO consolidated Swiss sanctions list (UN-aligned); (2) EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (3) UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions list; (4) US OFAC SDN list; (5) Swiss PEP definition under Article 2a AMLA. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory upon identification of a PEP, close relative or close associate, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, senior-management approval and ongoing monitoring. For this low-risk ISIC 4646 wholesale distribution business, simplified customer due diligence may apply after full UBO verification; however, sanctions screening and adverse-media checks remain compulsory at onboarding and on a continuous basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Central Business Name Index) at www.zefix.ch and the cantonal Commercial Register electronic filing portal Regix operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Article 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and Article 30 of the Commercial Register Ordinance, the company name must be expressed in one of the Swiss national languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or in a customary foreign language, including English, provided it is not misleading; any non-Latin trade name, including Chinese characters, must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; the legal-form suffix AG (Aktiengesellschaft) or SA is mandatory; the name must be clearly distinguishable from all existing registered names and must not contravene Article 31 of the Federal Act on the Protection of the Swiss Coat of Arms (Swissness restrictions).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bund, Eidgenossenschaft, Confederation (sovereign/public-authority designation requiring special concession)
Swiss, Schweiz, Suisse, Helvetia (territorial designation requiring compliance with Swissness trademark statutes and public-interest justification)
Bank, Sparkasse, Banque (requires FINMA banking licence under the Banking Act)
Versicherung, Assurances, Insurance (requires FINMA insurance supervisory licence)
Trust, Treuhand, Fiduciaire (requires cantonal professional authorisation where regulated)
National, Fonds, Börse, Clearing (misleading public-authority or financial-market connotations requiring prior authorisation)
Municipality, canton or federal-state names without the written consent of the competent authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is entered via Regix in the cantonal pre-register and is held for 180 days; it may be renewed once by a new reservation application filed before expiry. In case of rejection, the Cantonal Commercial Register Office issues a written negative ruling with reasons; the applicant may within 30 days of notification file an administrative appeal with the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority and simultaneously submit an amended alternative name proposal to prevent delay. A subsequent appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht, St. Gallen) and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht, Lausanne), each within 30 days of the respective ruling. To preserve the incorporation timetable, three substitute names are reserved in parallel and the corporate-form suffix and share capital are fixed before the name search.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited. A domiciliation or virtual office is acceptable at the registration stage in most cantons, including Zurich, Zug and Geneva, using a licensed domiciliation provider; however, for an operational international wholesale distributor of optical frames, the Swiss tax authorities (ESTV/FTA), social security inspectorates (AHV/SUVA) and the VAT administration require genuine economic substance, namely a leased physical office or dedicated serviced-office suite, documented accounting and filing infrastructure, decision-making by Swiss resident directors or authorised managers, and employment substance proportionate to turnover. A pure letterbox structure may trigger seat re-qualification, denial of DTA benefits, VAT adjustments and administrative fines; the recommended configuration is a serviced office with a designated physical suite, part-time administrative presence and full Swiss records retention.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 12% probability per fiscal year of an unannounced on-site visit by the cantonal tax inspection unit or AHV social security inspectors, rising to approximately 25% upon VAT data mismatches, invoicing anomalies or changes in UBOs; the Commercial Register Office itself does not perform routine physical inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht/Code des obligations, SR 220), Arts. 620–643 (stock corporation formation), 626 (required Articles of Association content), 632 (minimum capital and paid-up rule), 643 (Commercial Register filing); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411), Arts. 1–56
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt/Registre du commerce) of the registered office canton, coordinated with the Federal Commercial Register maintained under oversight of the Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) including the Declaration of Formation and the Articles of Association (Statuten/Statuts), filed electronically by the notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nominal share capital of at least CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 (20% of each share's nominal value) must be paid up in cash before registration; funds must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss-regulated bank and evidenced by a bank confirmation letter (Bankbestätigung) valid for 20 days
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the share capital of CHF 100,000 be subscribed in full and that CHF 50,000 be paid into the blocked escrow account of the company at (bank name), Switzerland, as evidenced by the bank confirmation letter dated (date); RESOLVED that the registered office of the company be and is hereby fixed at (street, postcode, place), Switzerland; RESOLVED that (name) be and is hereby appointed Chairman and member of the Board of Directors, together with (name) and (name), each exercising individual signature authority; RESOLVED that (name) be appointed Chief Executive Officer with individual signature authority and that (name) be appointed authorized officer (Prokurist) with collective signature authority; RESOLVED that the Board file the incorporation with the Commercial Register through the acting notary and that all ancillary acts be hereby ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarize the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (öffentliche Notarin/Notar), locally certified for deed certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Swiss-chartered notary to draft the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association in German, French, or Italian as applicable. The founders execute the deed in person or by written power of attorney; a cash contribution plan and capital payment schedule must be attached. The notary verifies the identity of founders, the lawfulness of the corporate purpose (wholesale distribution of optical frames), and compliance with Art. 626 OR.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Passport or Swiss ID of each founder and signatory director
Extract of the debt enforcement register (Betreibungsregister) for all founders domiciled in Switzerland
Declaration of acceptance of office by each director (Art. 627 OR)
Power of attorney if any founder appears by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the deed, amend the Articles or capitalization evidence and re-execute; no loss of priority if cured within the 20-day validity of the bank confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit minimum paid-up capital in a blocked escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated bank (e.g., cantonal bank, UBS, or licensed private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the company's name ('Gründungskonto') and deposit at least CHF 50,000 representing 20% of each subscribed share's nominal value. Instruct the bank to issue a formal bank confirmation (Bankbestätigung) confirming the deposit is at the free disposal of the company only upon Commercial Register registration. The confirmation must be dated no earlier than 20 days before filing.
required_dossiers: Protocol of share subscription with allocation of shares to founders
Founders' payment orders and proof of source of funds
Bank confirmation letter (Bankbestätigung) for the blocked escrow balance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines the confirmation, supplement lawful origin-of-funds documentation (e.g., bank statements, contracts) under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and re-deposit or top-up the funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the incorporation application with the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via secured notary-facilitated electronic filing (TEREOS platform)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to transmit the deed, Articles, bank confirmation, and director acceptances to the Commercial Register of the registered office canton. The filing must include the declaration that legal organization of the company is ensured (Art. 643 OR). Pay the applicable registration fee (approximately CHF 400–800 federal-cantonal composite).
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation with Articles of Association
Bank confirmation letter (Bankbestätigung)
Declaration of formation confirming subscription and payment plan
List of directors and signatory powers
Certificate of debt enforcement solvency (Betreibungsregisterauszug) if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a deficiency letter (Verfügung), cure deficiencies within 30 days, generally by supplementary notarial declaration; appeal any refusal to the competent supervisory authority within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain legal personality and effect official publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register in coordination with the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt/SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon entry in the Commercial Register, the company acquires legal personality (Art. 643 para. 1 OR). The Registrar publishes the incorporation details (date, legal form, seat, purpose, capital, signature rules) in the SHAB. Immediately after publication, request the updated Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug) to verify the company's active status and authorized signatories.
required_dossiers: No new filing; rely on Register entry
Registered address verification and corporate documents for bank and agency use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains errors, petition the Commercial Register office for rectification within the statutory objection period; correct data errors at no cost before first annual return.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration fiscal, social insurance, and trade notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV), cantonal tax authority, AHV Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse), SUVA, and municipal trade/police authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for VAT with the FTA (mandatory if annual turnover exceeds CHF 250,000; optional below); register as an employer with the cantonal AHV Compensation Office and with SUVA for mandatory accident insurance; enroll employees in the occupational pension fund (BVG/LPP); confirm the commercial premises for industrial safety and fire insurance with the cantonal building insurance body; obtain a business registration certificate (Handelsregister occupancy confirmation) where required by municipal regulation.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (post-registration)
Form for VAT registration (Formulaire 2010/Registration Form)
Employer registration form for AHV/SUVA (Anneldung Arbeitgeber)
Occupational pension fund declaration (BVG/LPP)
Copy of lease or title deed for the warehouse and office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or insurance registrations are delayed, file retroactive applications with written justification; avoid retroactive liability by submitting VAT and AHV registration within 30 days of failing the CHF 250,000 turnover threshold or hiring the first employee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – wholesale distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames (ISIC 4646) is an unrestricted commercial activity; no cantonal industrial or manufacturing license required. General trade facilitation is the remit of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and the cantonal trade office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license is required for wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames; the Commercial Register entry and, if applicable, municipal economic activity registration (Wirtschaftsregister) constitute the sole administrative prerequisites.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU), with cantonal environmental enforcement agencies
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the undertaking is purely an importer/wholesaler with no manufacturing, chemical processing, or effluent-producing activity; therefore no EIA screening under Art. 10a of the Environmental Protection Act (USG, SR 814.01) or Annex to the EIA Ordinance (SR 814.011) is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions are generated on-site; the operation must comply with the general duty of environmental care (USG Art. 1) and the Waste Ordinance (VVEA, SR 814.600), requiring segregated disposal of damaged acetate frames and packaging; the storage premises must comply with the Climate and Innovation Act (SR 814.31) energy-efficiency obligations for building services and with the Chemicals Ordinance (SR 813.11) if any cleaning solvents are stored.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Cantonal Fire Insurance Institution (Kantonaler Gebäudeversicherung/GVA) for the warehouse and office premises, including fire alarm and extinguisher inspection; structural load clearance from the cantonal building authority confirming floor loading capacity for palletized storage; workplace safety inspection and accident prevention review by SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund) under Art. 82 of the Accident Insurance Act (UVG); municipal leicht end-of-leasing certificate ensuring premises meet the Swiss Energy Ordinance (EnV) for lighting and heating.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV) - VAT Main Division and Federal Direct Tax Division; Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG/FOCBS) for export evidence; official e-portal: https://www.estv.admin.ch and VAT e-services „MWST online / TVA-TP“; cantonal tax administrations (e.g. Steueramt Zug) for cantonal and municipal corporate income and capital tax, which receive the registration ex officio via the commercial register data transfer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation of the Swiss Aktiengesellschaft in the Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt), the Federal Statistical Office (BFS/UST) automatically allocates the Swiss Business Identifier „UID“ in the ZEFIX central name index (format CHE-123.456.789, Federal Act on the Swiss Business Identifier, UIDG). The UID with extension „MWST“ constitutes the VAT number. VAT registration is filed with the ESTV through the „Anmeldung zur Mehrwertsteuerpflicht / Umsatzmeldung“ e-form (Art. 66-67 LTVA/MWSTG). Non-established foreign enterprises must additionally designate a Swiss fiscal representative domiciled in Switzerland, who is jointly and severally liable for the VAT obligations (Art. 67 para. 3 LTVA). The Cantonal Tax Office registers the AG for federal, cantonal and municipal corporate income, and capital taxes by way of commercial-register notification; separate notifications are due for the OASI/AVS compensation fund and for Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends at the statutory 35% rate, subject to treaty reduction or reclaim.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Swiss AG is mandatorily a corporate taxpayer at all three levels - federal direct tax at 8.5% of net profit (effective approximately 7.83% after the tax-deduction rule) and cantonal/municipal profit and capital taxes at combined effective rates of approximately 11% in Zug to approximately 20% in higher-tax cantons. Resident companies are taxable on worldwide income, with the exemption method applied to foreign permanent establishments and foreign immovable property (Art. 52 DBG / Art. 20 StHG). The AG has no shareholder pass-through; profits are taxed at entity level and dividend distributions are subject to the Swiss 35% withholding tax unless the participation exemption or a treaty applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law provides no check-the-box or partnership-transparency election for a stock company; the legal-form classification is mandatory. Available elections and reliefs: (i) VAT group taxation (Mehrwertsteuer-Gruppenbesteuerung, Art. 12 LTVA) for closely-merged Swiss entities consolidating into one taxpayer; (ii) flat-rate input VAT deduction under the Saldosteuersatz procedure for eligible SMEs with turnover below CHF 5,005,000; (iii) election between the calendar year and a commercial fiscal year, subject to tax authority approval; (iv) participation relief (Qualified Participation Deduction) under Art. 70 DBG and Art. 28 StHG for dividend and capital-gain income meeting the 10% shareholding and CHF 1,000,000 thresholds; (v) partial deemed tax credit (Teilbesteuerungsverfahren) for qualifying participation dividends effective 1 January 2025; (vi) transitional status-company reliefs (holding, domiciliary, mixed) following the TRAF 2020 corporate tax reform; (vii) hybrid-mismatch limitation rules derived from the Swiss DBA-Paket and ATAD without any entity-election mechanism. No fiscal unity or group taxation exists for Swiss corporate income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT / MWST / TVA / IVA) under the Federal Act on Value Added Tax of 12 June 2009 (LTVA/MWSTG), aligned with EU VAT principles but outside the EU customs and VAT union; general excise and customs law remains inapplicable to optical frames beyond standard import duties.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 global annual taxable turnover for resident enterprises (increased from CHF 100,000 effective 1 January 2025, Art. 10 para. 2 LTVA). Non-resident enterprises must register when Swiss-source service turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year or when distance/goods supplies into Switzerland exceed CHF 250,000 per year. Voluntary registration without threshold is permitted; registration may be waived below the threshold unless input VAT refund claims are sought.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory tax-authority API, and no digital stamping regime applies in Switzerland. The ESTV accepts structured electronic invoices (Peppol BIS 3.0, EIC, eBill, EDI) for VAT audit purposes; invoices issued to the federal administration (B2G) must be delivered electronically through the Peppol/eBill channel from 1 January 2026 under the Swiss Confederation e-invoicing strategy. All VAT-relevant records, including export evidence, must be produced electronically on audit and retained for 10 years (Art. 81 LTVA).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of acetate eyeglass frames qualify for the 0% VAT rate with full deduction of input VAT (echte Steuerbefreiung, Art. 23 para. 2 ch. 1 LTVA) where the goods physically leave Swiss territory for a foreign customer. The exporter must hold the electronic Swiss customs export declaration issued by BAZG and, for goods destined to EU business customers under the reporting procedure (Meldeverfahren, Art. 54 LTVA), a signed Lieferbescheinigung (delivery certificate) obtained from the importing customer. Failing physical export, the supply is domestic and taxable at the standard 8.1% rate, including goods placed into a Swiss consignment or fulfillment warehouse. Services supplied to foreign wholesale customers are outside Swiss VAT under the B2B place-of-supply rule (Art. 8 LTVA). Switzerland maintains no foreign-exchange controls and imposes no statutory export-proceeds repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark below reflects the schema default and standard Swiss banking and trade-finance practice for outward remittance collection evidenced by SWIFT MT103 statements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Swiss customs export declaration (BAZG e-dec/Passar) including the export approval number and the Ausfuhrschein confirmation
Bill of Lading (ocean) / Air Waybill / CMR rail-road consignment note evidencing physical movement across the Swiss border
Commercial invoice (DE/EN/FR) and packing list cross-referenced to the customs declaration
Lieferbescheinigung (delivery certificate, Art. 54 LTVA) for EU-bound goods under the reporting procedure or the foreign customs import declaration (e.g. EU SAD/ATLAS import document)
Bank SWIFT MT103 / inward remittance certificate evidencing foreign payment collection
Transport insurance certificate and warehouse release documents supporting the complete export chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV verifies export zero-rating through document-based audits of the BAZG export records and Lieferbescheinigungen. Missing or contradictory export proof triggers retroactive reassessment of VAT at the 8.1% standard rate plus statutory default interest published by the Federal Department of Finance under Art. 87 LTVA (approximately 4-5% p.a.) and the clawback of input VAT previously deducted on the export supply. Fraudulent zero-rating claims constitute VAT evasion (Art. 97 LTVA), with fines up to four times the evaded tax in willful cases and up to one times in negligent cases; procedural violations (Art. 96 LTVA) attract administrative fines up to CHF 8,000; criminal tax fraud (Steuerbetrug) using forged documents is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years and monetary penalties (Art. 100 LTVA / Art. 186 DBG). The right to assess expires after 5 years, extended to 10 years where evasion is established (Art. 42 LTVA); export records must be kept for 10 years (Art. 81 LTVA).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB); monetary authority and FX statistics supervisor. No separate foreign-exchange-control administration exists. Banking and anti-money-laundering supervision is exercised by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). The Swiss International Financial Services Standard (SIF) framework and the CDB Ordinance govern client due diligence in onboarding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full capital and current account convertibility. Switzerland imposes no exchange-control approvals on inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, trade payments, profit remittances, or liquidation proceeds. Dividends paid by a Swiss AG are subject to the federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) of 35%, reduced or refundable under an applicable double taxation treaty; interest on shareholder loans is generally not subject to Swiss withholding tax if at arm's length. No minimum local-currency holding period or repatriation approval applies to the eyewear distribution business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland has no statutory obligation to surrender, convert, or repatriate export proceeds within any prescribed timeline. Receivables from the wholesale export of ophthalmic eyewear frames may remain in foreign currency in domestic or foreign accounts. Only ex-post statistical reporting to the SNB under its statistical data-collection ordinance (SR 932.111) may apply once foreign assets or liabilities of the Swiss resident enterprise exceed the statutory thresholds, and this is informational, not a convertibility or custody control.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) plus Operational Account in CHF/EUR/USD
Operational Account and Payment Clearing Account
Operational Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with strict legal constraints. FINMA-licensed fintech entities holding a banking licence under Art. 1b Banking Act may accept up to CHF 100 million in client deposits without paying interest, making them compliant for low-balance operating flows but not for capital escrow or material trade settlement. Offshore EMIs licensed in the EU or UK are not permitted to conduct deposit-taking or payment services for Swiss residents in a cross-border manner without a Swiss banking or FinSA licensing gateway; they are viable only as front-end payment facilitators for Platform_Pay collections, with a nightly sweep to a FINMA-regulated Tier-1 account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence at the onboarding interview is effectively mandatory for the ultimate beneficial owner and at least one authorised signatory of a foreign-controlled Swiss AG. Remote video identification is accepted for low-risk natural persons only and is generally not accepted by Tier-1 banks for corporate accounts when the UBO is a non-resident. Swiss notarised signatures, apostilled corporate documents, and a prior bank reference may reduce the interview length, but cannot fully waive the in-person meeting for a new non-resident client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO with no prior Swiss banking relationship and no clear source of wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Handelsregisterauszug (commercial register extract), articles of association, group structure chart, passport or national ID of the UBO, banker's reference from a recognised foreign bank, source-of-wealth evidence (tax returns, sale agreements, inheritance documents, audited financial statements), Swiss office lease, payroll records, and any tax residence certificate of the UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party marketplace and platform payouts flowing through non-banking aggregators or payment facilitators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed wholesale distribution agreements with opticians and retail chains, purchase orders and pro-forma invoices, CMR/B/L/AWB transport documents, customs declarations, marketplace reconciliation statements, the platform's own licence or payment-stats confirmation, and a description of the counterparty's upstream beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade settlements to or from jurisdictions perceived as high-risk (Hong Kong SAR, UAE free zones, Singapore intermediaries) for eyewear stock purchases
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Manufacturer qualification file, import licences and customs import declarations, end-customer flow diagrams, certificate of origin for acetate frames, trademark licensing or brand-authorisation evidence, credit-insurance agency reports on the counterparty, and a Swiss substance file proving commercial rationale for the routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: At incorporation, the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital is funded by a related party or trust with an opaque structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-blocked account confirmation (Sperrkonto-Bestätigung), trust deed and letter of wishes, professional legal opinion identifying the economic settlor and beneficiaries, TIEA or DTT residence certificates for all intermediate entities, and the bank's 'know-your-client' disclosure questionnaire showing the funding chain down to natural persons.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital is wired by SWIFT MT103 (customer credit) into the Swiss Sperrkonto (blocked account) at incorporation, with the bank issuing the required blocking confirmation. Subsequent shareholder loans or capital increases are cleared via MT103/MT202 through the Swiss SIC/EuroSIC system; the bank records the statutory payment-statistics declaration for the SNB under the purpose 'Erhöhung des Aktienkapitals' (capital increase) or 'Zuschuss / Darlehen' (shareholder contribution/loan). No exchange-control approval is required, but injections exceeding CHF 1 million trigger enhanced due diligence, requiring a board resolution and the matched funding-chain documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for wholesale payments in EUR, USD, and CHF, with onward clearing through SIC, EuroSIC, TARGET2, and US correspondent banks. For risk-mitigated trade, irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 and documentary collections under URC 522 are used; the standard payment profile for acetate eyewear frame shipments is 30% advance by MT103 and 70% against presentation of shipping documents. Platform_Pay proceeds are settled via acquiring banks through SEPA Credit Transfer and local card/wallet rails, with a nightly sweep into the Swiss operational account to maintain single-point liquidity concentration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, EUR/USD) with FINMA-regulated Swiss banks under ISDA 2002 or local master agreements, unrestricted in maturity or notional
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps (CCS) matching CHF funding against USD and EUR trade disbursements
Plain-vanilla European FX options purchased from Swiss and top-tier EU banks, structured to avoid margin-call exposure on the Swiss AG
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted emerging-market currencies (e.g., USD/CNY, USD/INR, USD/BRL) executed via Swiss bank desks, permissible as the SNB imposes no offshore NDF restrictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary Annual General Meeting (AGM) and adoption of annual financial statements, profit appropriation and discharge of the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of shareholders (internal corporate body; minutes of the AGM are recorded in the corporate minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance-sheet date; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year (within four months for listed Swiss issuers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative strike-off exists for a missed AGM; a shareholder may petition the competent court to convene the AGM and the Board is exposed to personal liability for resulting damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and net wealth tax return (Federal, cantonal and communal taxation) with signed annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered-office canton (e.g., Zug: Kantonales Steueramt); Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) receives the federal corporate income tax assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year basis: return generally due by 31 March or 30 June of the following year depending on the canton; written extensions may be requested; assessed taxes are payable within 30 days after service of the assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge and late-payment interest at the statutory variable rate, penal surcharge for wilful or negligent under-reporting; persistent non-payment triggers tax execution leading to enforcement against assets and bankruptcy-liquidation of the AG; no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT) return and VAT balance settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an annual VAT reporting period: filed within 60 days after the end of the tax period (1 March following a calendar-year period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing reminder fees, late-payment interest at the variable statutory rate, administrative fines for each filing omission, and assessment based on taxable basis by the FTA in the absence of a return; no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax statement and remittance (35% Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends declared at the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Withholding Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Dividend withholding tax is declared and paid within 30 days after the coupon/dividend due date; if no dividend is declared, no payment or filing arises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues from the due date on unpaid withholding tax; penal consequences for wilful failure can include a criminal fine plus restitution of tax; no administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer wage declaration and settlement of AHV/AVS social insurance contributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compensation Fund of the registered office (AHV-Ausgleichskasse) and competent cantonal social insurance collection agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AHV/AVS contributions are remitted monthly or quarterly; the annual wage statement is due by 31 January following the contribution year, subject to the compensation-fund filing schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest and administrative fines for late wage statements; employer is liable for unpaid employee contribution deductions and may be subject to criminal prosecution for failure to pay contributions; no administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit is mandatory for a Swiss AG whose equity securities are listed on a regulated stock exchange or which exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: total assets CHF 20 million; net revenue CHF 40 million; 250 full-time employees on average. A limited statutory audit is mandatory for an AG with more than 10 full-time employees; an AG with an average workforce of 10 employees or fewer may waive the limited audit by unanimous shareholder resolution.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO Art. 957–963c) defines Swiss statutory financial reporting (Swiss GAAP); Swiss GAAP FER is used for consolidated financial statements; IFRS Accounting Standards for listed issuers and publicly held debt securities; unlisted SMEs may apply the simplified CO presentation unless consolidated IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO return is filed with a Swiss central registry for a non-listed AG. The Board must maintain the share register and, before every ordinary AGM, verify all transfers and outstanding registered shares. For bearer shares or any shareholder holding more than 25% of the company's share capital, the Board must identify and record the beneficial owner in accordance with Swiss anti-money-laundering due-diligence practice and must be able to produce such records to the authorities on demand; this is an event-driven and AGM-confirmation duty rather than a standalone annual filing.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800–5,500 per year for a professional domiciliation/registered-office service in a low-tax commercial canton such as Zug, including registered agent assistance, correspondence forwarding and basic corporate secretarial support; higher for physical office and dedicated fiduciary in-house services.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–9,000 per year for a limited statutory audit of a small AG; USD 15,000–40,000 per year for a full ordinary statutory audit of a wholesale distributing AG with international volume and inventory complexity.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
